Those bullets are genuinely the best writing in the zone — «Policy и Middleware — одно и то же» — нет. Middleware выполняется раньше...» is exactly the plain-language definition the body needed. So the answer to the zone question is: it is not that 4.3k words are too few to teach anything, it is that the explanatory prose is all in the last screen of each file, and the body above it is a code dump. The material for the missing leads already exists inside the article — it just needs to be moved up.
- **Every concept is anchored to another framework the reader may not know.** Content Type is «Аналог таблицы в БД + Prisma Model + NestJS Entity». Policy is «аналог Guard в NestJS». Lifecycle Hooks are «Аналог Prisma middleware или Mongoose pre/post hooks». Middleware is «аналог Koa/Express middleware». Two of the seven articles carry a full Strapi-vs-NestJS comparison table. This is a good habit turned into the only habit: an analogy is a shortcut for readers who have the reference, and nothing at all for readers who do not. Every one needs to follow a first-principles sentence, not replace it.
- **Version drift inside single files.** Article 01 tells the reader v5 removed the nested `attributes` wrapper, and its own REST example above returns the v4 `data`/`attributes` shape; article 03's Dynamic Zone response does the same; article 05's is-admin policy calls `strapi.entityService.findOne` (the v4 API that articles 02, 04 and 07 all say was replaced). Articles are read out of order, so nothing tells a reader landing on 03 or 05 that the example they are copying is a major version behind. Every code block in this zone needs a version marker in its first comment line.

**Прочее:** B is the zone's best score (4.0 flat — 3 long sentences in 14 files, no bureaucratic register, no genitive chains). C at 1.3 and D at 1.4 are the worst two scores I would expect to see anywhere on this site, and they measure the same defect: not dense prose, but absent prose. Volume is not the problem the way the zone brief framed it — 4.3k words could teach this material; the issue is that ~70% of those words are inside code fences and ~90% of what remains is the closing pitfalls list, so the average article body is 10-30 words of explanation for 600 words of code. Fixing this zone means adding, not rewriting: a lead paragraph per section (~150 words x 33 sections), lifted largely from the pitfalls lists that already exist. EN and RU are near-identical translations of the same skeleton, so every finding above applies to both locales; EN is not harder than RU here (F 3.9) precisely because there is so little prose to be hard.

### system-design (вопросы) — системный рефактор

- The `Senior nuance` dumping ground WAS inherited, just without the label. All 25 answers use one fixed shape: `### <thesis heading>` -> 1-3 prose paragraphs -> code -> one or two closing paragraphs that pack the three or four hardest facts of the topic into a single 45-78-word sentence -> `**Common pitfall:**`. In 16 of 25 EN answers the last prose paragraph before the pitfall is literally one sentence, and in 21 of 25 it is 40+ words. That paragraph is where nearly all of the 256 flagged over-long sentences live, and it is the one paragraph in each answer with no example, no code and no numbers. Fixing this one slot would move the flag density more than any other change.
- The house sentence is `<framing clause>: <fact A>, so <fact B> — <fact C>, <fact D>` — a colon followed by an em-dash-chained tail. The punctuation already marks the seams, so almost every over-limit sentence can be split at its own existing colon and em-dashes into 3-4 sentences with zero content loss. This is a mechanical fix, not a rewrite.
- The `### <thesis>` heading is a genuinely good pattern and is the main thing propping up Rubric C — every one of the 25 headings is a real claim, not a topic label. But the first body paragraph then restarts from zero instead of continuing the heading, usually with a negation or framing warm-up: `The naive model —`, `The naive answer —`, `The naive heuristic (...)`, `The part that makes this harder`, `The part that actually trips teams up`, `The whole point of X is`, `There are two separate problems here`, `At small scale, X wins`. Nine of 25 answers open this way, and in four of them (q-4, q-11, q-13, q-18) the specific thing the question asked for lands only after the code block.
- The `[Article Name]` bracket-reference habit was NOT inherited: the bank contains zero plain-text bracket references. It also contains zero real links and zero diagrams — in the one topic where the site's diagram primitive would pay off most (fan-out via pub-sub in q-24, host/remote isolation in q-18, compliance-aware failover in q-22, the three-tier token hierarchy in q-15). Four or five diagrams would absorb the densest closing paragraphs directly.
- RU is the shorter and plainer locale; EN is the harder one. EN is 11% longer (6952 vs 6251 words), has 14 more over-limit sentences, and carries all the idiom load. But RU pays for it in two other ways: English nouns inflected with an apostrophe (tree-shake'ить, remote'у, tombstone'ов, broadcast'ов) and untranslated English noun phrases sitting bare in Russian sentences (blast radius, sparse fieldsets, ingestion pipeline, happy-path, fire-and-forget, drop-oldest, комплаенс-регион).

**Прочее:** The `**Common pitfall:**` block is the best-written part of the bank — a concrete wrong choice plus its concrete consequence, present in all 25 answers — but it is itself a single 40-50-word em-dash sentence every time, so it inherits the same B defect. Code quality is otherwise high: self-contained, commented at the non-obvious lines, no cross-example state; the only real E defects are line width (~120 lines over 82 chars, RU worse than EN) and mislabelled fence languages. Bureaucratic RU markers are essentially absent (no «является», «осуществляется», «в случае если»); the RU problem is calque, not officialese. Question stems sometimes expand an abbreviation the answer then uses bare (BFF, CSP, SRI, ABAC), which is why those are not in the unexpanded list — but TTL, CDN, SSE, SSR, SSG, ORM, CI and DOM are expanded nowhere in either locale.

### system-design (статьи) — точечные правки

- Abbreviations are expanded once per ZONE, not once per FILE — and the zone is read out of order. TTL is expanded only in article 03 but used in 02, 06, 07, 09, 11 and 12; CDN is expanded only in 02 but used in 01, in article 06's own title, and in 11 and 12; SPOF and NFR are expanded only in 01 but used in 10 and 11; DLQ only in 05 but used in 10; CQRS only in 04 but used as the framing of article 12's whole search section. This single habit accounts for most of the 151 mechanical abbreviation flags and for the A average of 3.0. The fix is one gloss-on-first-use pass per file, not new content.
- Plain-text bracket cross-references that look like links and are not. The renderer (src/components/theory/ArticleRenderer.tsx) runs `marked` with no reference-link resolution, so `[Chat System]` reaches the phone as literal bracketed text. Article 11 has 9 in prose plus ~11 more inside ```txt blocks; article 12 has 12; articles 09 and 10 have 5-6 each. Worse, the bracket text does not match the article titles it points at (`[WebSockets]` vs the actual "WebSockets and Realtime Systems"; `[File Storage and CDN]` in the RU files vs the RU title "File Storage и CDN"), so even manual sidebar-hunting fails. Either make them real markdown links or drop the brackets and name the article in prose.
- The `Senior-нюанс:` / `Senior nuance:` paragraph is used as a dumping ground: it typically carries the article's three or four hardest facts in one 35-50-word sentence with two nested parentheticals. It appears 20+ times across the zone and is where almost every over-length sentence lives (01 availability nines, 02 TLS termination and /health, 03 in-process cache, 05 exactly-once, 06 pre-signed URL security, 07 SSE, 11 time allocation). Keep the label — it is a useful signal of depth — but split the payload into 2-3 sentences.
- Sections that open with a deferral instead of an answer. Article 02's first sentence is «Базовое различие ... разобрано в [System Design Fundamentals]»; article 11 §"Общая структура" opens «Эта последовательность была подробно описана в [...]»; article 11 §"SQL vs NoSQL" opens «Framework для выбора был подробно разобран в [Database Scaling]»; article 09's intro closes on the same move. A reader arriving from search is told where the content is not before receiving any content. Move the pointer to the end of the paragraph and lead with the fact — in every one of these cases the fact is already sitting in the same sentence's second half.
- The EN locale is consistently harder than the RU it was written from, and not only because of the expected ~19% length inflation. Over-limit sentence rates roughly double (article 01: 12% RU → 27% EN; article 02: 20% → 43%), and F is 3 or below in all 12 files. Two causes: (a) RU sentences that were readable at 30 words become 45-word EN ones without being re-broken; (b) calques that produce non-English — "serve a multiple of the users" (03), "The practical consequence to fix here" (02), "Ordering — guarantees that cost something" (05) — plus idioms above B2 ("a bag of buzzwords", "close the door to a senior signal", "wide but shallow", "the same sin as", "reaching for a Redis lock"). The EN files need a sentence-splitting pass; the RU files mostly do not.
- Wide two-column ASCII layouts inside ```txt blocks. Article 03's «Без кеша | С кешом», article 04's «До шардинга | После шардинга» and article 10's final-architecture diagram run 68-93 characters wide. The site renders these in a horizontally scrolling `<pre>`, so on a phone the second column is only reachable by side-scrolling — which destroys the side-by-side comparison the block exists to make. Every one of the 24 files has at least one line of 75-94 characters inside a fenced block.
- Meta-references to the article's own revision history leak into the body text: «старая версия статьи правильно его обозначала» (ru/07:43, en/07:42 — in the opening sentence of that article's central section) and «(старая версия статьи)» / "(the old version of this article)" (ru/10:44, en/10:43). The reader has never seen an old version; these clauses are pure noise sitting in high-value positions.

**Прочее:** Four RU text-corruption typos where a non-Cyrillic character replaced a Cyrillic one: 低 for «низкую» (11:304), `bagажа` (11:342), `konце` (12:300), `ресharding` (04:100) — all four are byproducts of the zone-wide habit of declining Latin nouns with Cyrillic endings (`worker'ов`, `consumer'ами`, `bottleneck'ом`, 30+ instances). Also: ru/11:123 has a grammar error («Один и тот же функциональный требование»), and ru/12:362 has an English preposition in a Russian heading («Общие паттерны across всех 12 задач»). Register is inconsistent across the zone: articles 01-03 address the reader as «ты», article 11 uses «вы» 20 times. Every RU article title is untranslated English, which the rubric flags under G; I scored it as a zone-wide baseline rather than docking each file separately. Verdict is targeted-fixes rather than systemic-refactor because C/D/E average 3.7-3.8 — the concept sequencing, diagrams and code examples are genuinely strong and no article needs rewriting; the EN locale is the closest call, since its sentence-length problem is present in all 12 files.

### tdd (вопросы) — системный рефактор

- The dominant structural habit: where content/questions/testing.json introduces N parallel concepts as a bulleted list, tdd.json runs them together inside one paragraph with bolded run-in labels. Red / Green / Refactor (q-1), the four qualities of a good unit test (q-2), the three AAA steps (q-4), the three pyramid levels (q-5), the four test doubles (q-9), the three layers of an API endpoint (q-14), the four test smells (q-23), the three parts of the flaky-test strategy (q-25). This one habit produces nearly all 40+ over-long paragraphs the script flags and every wall of theory in the file. Converting these to lists — no wording changes at all — would fix most of B and D at once.
- Every mid-level and senior answer contains one 'decision rule' sentence delivered as a single 60-96-word chain of semicolon-separated branches: q-7 ('the decision comes down to three questions...'), q-9 ('the choice depends on what the test actually needs to prove...'), q-18 (the two-axis risk framework), q-19 (the incremental-CI approach), q-22 ('the practical, senior-level resolution...'). These are the most valuable sentences in the bank and the least readable ones; each is a table pretending to be prose.
- The bank argues from named authorities and named patterns without ever introducing them: TDD itself, BDD, DHH, Uncle Bob, Michael Feathers, London/Detroit/Chicago schools, AST, DI. Well-known-inside-the-community names are treated as public knowledge, while genuinely obscure pattern names that the author chose to teach (seam, characterization test, Assertion Roulette, Mystery Guest, equivalent mutants) are all carefully defined. The file knows how to explain a term; it just does not notice which ones need it.
- Typographically the file is a straight import of an English source: 162 spaced hyphens and zero em-dashes in the RU locale, against 150 em-dashes in content/questions/testing.json#ru. In Russian a spaced hyphen does not signal a clause break, so on a phone every parenthetical aside has to be re-parsed. Four RU headings are also left fully in English.

**Прочее:** Overlap verdict: keep two banks, but stop re-teaching. 8 of 26 tdd entries cover the same ground as testing.json: pyramid (tdd-q-5 vs testing-q-1/q-16), test doubles (tdd-q-9 vs testing-q-6), snapshot (tdd-q-13 vs testing-q-9), mutation testing (tdd-q-19 vs testing-q-22), contract testing (tdd-q-20 vs testing-q-17), property-based (tdd-q-21 vs testing-q-18), micro-frontends (tdd-q-26 vs testing-q-21), shared-state/order dependence (tdd-q-23 vs testing-q-14). The two question banks never contradict each other — they agree everywhere and simply repeat, and tdd's versions of mutation testing and property-based testing are the deeper ones while testing's version of contract testing is. All actual contradictions in the topic live in content/quiz/testing.json (see the sibling report).
Recommendation: split by intent — tdd.json = process, design pressure, legacy adoption, pragmatism; testing.json = tools and techniques. For the four senior duplicates, keep whichever version is deeper and have the other cross-reference it. tdd-q-5 in particular is a near-verbatim second telling of testing-q-1, including the same three-example code shape, and is the clearest candidate for removal or reduction to a pointer.
Because neither `testing` nor `tdd` has a theory article, this bank is the site's only explanation of red-green-refactor, AAA and the test-double taxonomy — which is why the missing TDD expansion, the run-in walls in the junior entries (q-1 to q-5) and the total absence of any diagram are scored harder than they would be in a bank that sits behind an article.

### testing (вопросы+quiz) — системный рефактор

- Every answer in content/questions/testing.json ends with a 'practical trade-off' paragraph, and in ~20 of 25 entries that paragraph is a single 55-85-word sentence chaining three facts with em-dashes and semicolons (q-8, q-11, q-12, q-13, q-14, q-16, q-21, q-22, q-24). The structure is exactly what makes the bank senior-level and must stay; delivering each of them as one sentence is what pushes the EN long-sentence rate to 56%. Splitting each into three short sentences (or a short lead plus bullets) would halve that rate without dropping a single claim.
- The quiz bank was written independently of the question bank and shares neither its vocabulary nor its classifications. Three of fifteen items ask the same pyramid question (quiz-1, quiz-6, quiz-13), two ask the same stub-versus-mock question (quiz-2, quiz-7) with two different Russian vocabularies, and its positions on unit-versus-integration (quiz-11), spy semantics (quiz-12) and fake timers (quiz-9, quiz-15) all contradict content/questions/testing.json. It reads like a bank generated before the question bank existed and never reconciled with it.
- Tool-specific abbreviations are reliably expanded on first use (RTL, MSW, RUM, CDC, LCP, INP, CLS) while cross-cutting process abbreviations are never expanded at all (CI 8×, PR, KPI, APM, FID, MFE, DOM, БД/DB). The author expanded whatever felt like 'a tool name' and assumed everything from the daily workflow was common knowledge — but the target reader arriving from search has no theory article to fall back on.
- Not one diagram in the whole zone, across 40 entries. The only visual in the entire testing material is the ASCII pyramid in testing-quiz-1, and it is not inside a code fence, so it collapses in a proportional font. testing-q-16 (pyramid versus trophy) argues about two *shapes* for eight paragraphs and never draws either one.

**Прочее:** Overlap verdict: keep two banks, but split them by intent, not re-teach. 7 of 25 testing entries duplicate tdd entries almost fully — mutation testing (testing-q-22 / tdd-q-19), property-based (q-18 / q-21), contract testing (q-17 / tdd-q-20), micro-frontends (q-21 / tdd-q-26), snapshot (q-9 / tdd-q-13), pyramid (q-1, q-16 / tdd-q-5), test doubles (q-6 / tdd-q-9). The two *question* banks never contradict each other; they only repeat, and tdd's versions are usually the deeper ones. All real contradictions sit in the quiz bank, which disagrees with both question banks on the unit-vs-integration label (quiz-11), on what a spy is (quiz-12), and on whether fake timers are recommended (quiz-9, quiz-15 dismiss them; testing-q-12 and tdd-q-17 teach them).
Recommendation: testing.json = techniques and tooling, tdd.json = process and design pressure; cross-reference the four senior duplicates instead of explaining each twice; rewrite the quiz bank against the question banks' definitions and vocabulary.
Scoped verdict: content/questions/testing.json#ru needs targeted fixes only (it is the best file in the zone); #en needs a full sentence-splitting pass; content/quiz/testing.json needs a rewrite in both locales. The zone verdict is systemic-refactor because the last two are the majority of the zone's words.
One RU-only slip worth listing: q-16 and q-24 keep fully English headings («Testing Pyramid vs Testing Trophy», «Visual regression testing») while 21 of 25 headings are translated.

### typescript (вопросы) — точечные правки

- THE dominant pattern, and the one fix worth making: the bank is two different documents stitched together at typescript-q-45, and the seam is mechanical. Junior + middle (q-1..q-44) average 18-20 words per sentence in en / 15-17 in ru, with 21-23% / 11-14% of sentences over the limit. Senior + advanced (q-45..q-88) jump to 39-42 words per sentence in en / 35-39 in ru, with 69-75% / 57-66% over the limit. Nothing about the subject matter requires this: q-13 explains the `never` bottom type in 18-word sentences, while q-47 explains variance in 40-word ones. The seam is not gradual — it lands exactly on the difficulty boundary, which means it is an authoring-mode artifact, not a consequence of depth.
- Inside that seam, the single most repeated defect is the closing 'Common pitfall' / 'Частая ловушка' paragraph collapsing into one sentence. Junior/middle pitfalls are 2.3-2.5 sentences averaging 35-39 words total; senior/advanced pitfalls are 1.5-1.8 sentences averaging 66-73 words, with the longest sentence in the paragraph averaging 53-59 words. The recipe is always the same: 'Common pitfall: <gerund>ing X, then being confused when Y — <em-dash> the fix is Z rather than W.' All 44 senior/advanced entries follow it. Splitting that one paragraph per entry into 3-4 sentences would fix roughly a third of the bank's total long-sentence count without touching a single technical claim.
- A secondary but trust-damaging pattern: unedited drafting artifacts survive in three entries, all in the senior/advanced tier, all of the form '... actually <the opposite>'. typescript-q-82 reverses its own explanation of `Exact<T, Shape>` mid-sentence (both locales); typescript-q-49's code comment says a `const` literal is 'still string ... actually "red" for const' (en only — ru was cleaned); typescript-q-68 writes '// Error: Object literal may only specify known properties... actually here:' before quoting the real diagnostic (both locales). These are cheap to fix and they are the only places in 35k words where the text is actually wrong rather than merely long.
- Deferral leads. Several senior/advanced entries open by pointing at other entries instead of answering: 'This combines three mechanisms covered separately elsewhere' (q-61), 'All four are built on the same core mechanism' (q-53), 'These utility types build on the basics (Partial/Pick/Omit)' (q-23). In a bank whose entries are read standalone and out of order, a lead that references sibling entries spends the highest-value sentence in the answer on nothing.

**Прочее:** What this bank does right, and should become the style guide's positive examples: (1) every answer has the same three-part skeleton — one-paragraph direct answer, bolded mini-sections each paired with a 5-8 line code block, closing 'Common pitfall' that states the actual misconception rather than recapping; theory_walls is 0 in both locales, which no other shape achieves. (2) On rubric E for type-level code it is genuinely strong: ~25% of code blocks quote a real compiler diagnostic and another ~22% annotate the inferred type inline, including exact TS error codes (q-84 `error TS1262`, q-75/81/83 `error TS2589`) and full messages (q-54's `Argument of type '{ kind: "triangle"; ... }' is not assignable to parameter of type 'never'`, q-71's `this`-context error). Examples are self-contained and narrow — median code line is 27 chars, only 1.5-2% of junior/middle lines exceed 80. (3) Contrast pairs everywhere ('Without generics / With generics', 'Before TS 4.0 / After', BROKEN-vs-correct in q-71) give the reader a delta instead of a definition. Caveats on rubric E: advanced code blocks average 16.5 lines with 8.9% of lines over 80 chars (max 116, q-82's `ExactSelf` one-liner); a handful of 'Error' comments paraphrase the compiler rather than quote it (q-47, q-55); q-73's `onAny` snippet is a bare method body that dangles outside the class shown above it. On scoring: I treated each of the 88 entries as the real 'file' unit for rubric A, since a question bank is read entry-by-entry — that is why DI appears in the abbrev list (expanded in q-58, but used bare in q-67, where a reader arriving cold gets no expansion) while MFE, URI, HKT and AST do not (each is expanded inside its own entry). The verdict is targeted-fixes rather than systemic-refactor because the work is one repeatable operation applied to two known slots (lead sentence, closing pitfall paragraph) in the 44 senior/advanced entries, plus the ~6 one-off defects listed above — no restructuring, no content change, and the other 44 entries ship as they are.

### typescript (статьи+quiz) — точечные правки

- POSITIVE MODEL — articles 01-10 run a fixed five-beat rhythm that is the single best structural habit found anywhere on the site, and it is why flag density here is 7.0/1k, the lowest of any zone: (1) an H2 whose first sentence is a one-line plain-language definition with no warm-up ('Условный тип — это выражение уровня типов, которое работает как тернарный оператор'); (2) an ASCII ```txt``` box that shows the shape before any prose expands it; (3) a ❌-then-✅ code pair — the wrong way first, then the fix, in the SAME block; (4) the real compiler diagnostic pasted as an inline comment on the offending line, never paraphrased ('Duplicate identifier 'Point'', 'Object literal may only specify known properties', 'Type instantiation is excessively deep', 'Expression produces a union type that is too complex to represent', 'Object is possibly 'undefined''), ~41 verbatim diagnostics across the 11 EN files; (5) a closing 'Типичные ошибки на интервью' / 'Common Interview Traps' section of 6-7 bullets, each shaped as quoted-misconception-then-correction. This is the same discipline that made question-bank q-1..q-44 the best material on the site, and it holds for all ten teaching articles instead of dropping halfway. It also keeps code blocks at one per ~90 words, so no idea travels more than a screen without something concrete to hold.
- THE SEAM IS BY GENRE, NOT BY POSITION — articles 01-10 are uniformly excellent (RU 01, 02, 06, 08, 09, 10 have literally zero long sentences), and every mechanical flag in the zone concentrates in file 11, the Q&A article: 11 theory walls, 17 long paragraphs, 21 over-limit sentences in EN (7.1%) against 0-3 in every other file. The cause is measurable: file 11 carries 4146 words on 17 code blocks (one per ~244 words) while articles 01-10 average one per ~90 words. Beat (2) of the rhythm — the ```txt``` box — disappears entirely, and beats (3) and (4) survive only occasionally. File 11 is also the only file in the zone with no `<!-- verified: 2026-06-23 -->` header, suggesting it never went through the same review pass. Fixing it does not need new content, only the existing eight-flag list, the node16/bundler comparison and the isolatedModules answer converted into the ```txt``` boxes and ❌/✅ pairs that article 10 already contains.
- THE QUIZ BANK IS NOT WRITTEN TO THE SAME STANDARD AS ANYTHING ELSE IN THE ZONE, AND FIVE ITEMS ARE FACTUALLY BROKEN — quiz-20 contradicts articles 01 and 02 on unconstrained generic widening (and contradicts quiz-32, which uses the same function); quiz-25 asserts `true | false` differs from `boolean`, contradicting article 03; quiz-29's explanation states and then denies the same conclusion two sentences apart and its marked answer matches neither; quiz-30's explanation concedes that its own distractor D is also correct, contradicting article 10's list of eight strict flags; quiz-28's marked-correct option is captioned with the reason it is wrong. None of these would survive the articles' review bar. Separately, the bank quotes real compiler output only twice (quiz-14 'Cannot assign to 'name' because it is a readonly property', quiz-40 'Argument of type 'string | null' is not assignable to parameter of type 'string'') — the habit that makes the articles trustworthy is almost entirely absent here.
- ANSWER-SHAPE TELLS — correctIndex is not distributed: index 0 is correct in 26 of 38 items (68.4%), index 1 in 10, index 2 in 2, and index 3 is NEVER correct (0 of 38; expected ~9.5 each). A reader who notices this can score ~68% without reading the questions, and can eliminate the last option in every single item for free. Option length leaks the same way: the correct option is the strictly longest in 18/38 EN items (47.4%, plus 3 tied at longest = 21/38 at-or-tied) and 15/38 RU (39.5%, plus 2 tied); mean correct-option length is 61.4 chars against 47.8 for distractors in EN (+28%) and 63.9 vs 52.1 in RU (+23%). The tell is caused by a habit: the correct option is written as a full explanatory clause ('Interfaces support declaration merging, while type aliases do not') while distractors are stubs ('Type aliases are faster at runtime than interfaces').
- THE QUIZ REPEATS ITSELF INSTEAD OF COVERING THE ARTICLES — seven of 38 items (quiz-1, 6, 11, 21, 26, 31, 36 — 18%) ask the identical `interface` vs `type` declaration-merging fact, several with near-identical stems and explanations; add quiz-16 and it is 21% of the bank on one paragraph of article 01. Four items (13, 20, 27, 32) cover literal-vs-widened generic inference and five (10, 19, 22, 35, 37) cover the `typeof` guard. Meanwhile nine of the eleven articles have no quiz coverage at all: nothing on variance/contravariance, `satisfies`, `as const satisfies`, branded or phantom types, declaration files, module augmentation, `.d.ts`, template literal types, `infer`, exhaustiveness with `never`, `moduleResolution`, or `isolatedModules`. The bank behaves as if generated from a single seed topic rather than from the article set.
- EN IS SYSTEMATICALLY TRIMMED RELATIVE TO RU IN THE ARTICLES — the EN files silently drop content the RU files carry: en/09 has no 'Higher-Kinded Types симуляция' section and no `Tagged`/`TypedValue` phantom-type preamble; en/03 drops the `IsUnion` snippet and the `Mixed` index-signature note; en/04 drops `type EventHandler = \`on${Capitalize<DOMEvent>}\`` from Use Case 1 and the `RoutePath`/`RouteMethod` helpers from Use Case 5. Nothing is added in EN to compensate. The direction is unusual and worth a decision: elsewhere on the site EN is the harder read because it inflates; here EN is the shorter read because it omits. Where EN did rewrite rather than trim (en/07's `satisfies` 'bad' example), the rewrite replaced a visible half-finished thought with a silently incorrect claim, which is worse for the reader.

**Прочее:** Zone splits cleanly: the 22 article files are the strongest content audited so far and should be the style-guide exemplar (articles 01-10 in particular); the quiz is the weakest artefact in the zone and needs a correctness pass before a language pass. Quiz ids are non-contiguous — typescript-quiz-7 and -17 are absent from a 38-item file numbered 1-40. Every `question` field embeds a bare `typescript` line where a ``` fence should be (`"...shapes?\ntypescript\ninterface User {..."`), which will render as stray prose; several stems also glue two questions together (quiz-8, 20, 38 end with a second 'What is X?' after the code). Both are data defects, not writing defects, but they hit the reader on screen.

### web-performance (статьи+вопросы+quiz) — системный рефактор

- Metric acronyms are treated as if the reader already knows them, and almost never come with a number. Only 2 of the 16 articles (01-core-web-vitals and 08-interview-questions) expand every metric acronym they use; articles 02-07 use LCP/CLS/INP/TTFB/FCP/TTI/TBT with no expansion anywhere in the file, and only 01, 02 and 08 ever state a good value. In the question bank only 1 of the 4 entries that use LCP expands it, 1 of 5 for INP, 1 of 3 for CLS, 0 of 1 for FCP and FID. In the quiz bank, all 20 items go by without a single threshold: the strings 2.5s, 200ms and 0.1 do not appear in the file at all, even though 12 items are about LCP/INP/CLS/FID. Entries are read standalone, so 'it is expanded in article 01' does not help anyone.
- The question bank writes one mega-sentence per idea instead of one sentence per fact. Every answer in q-1..q-20 is exactly three prose paragraphs, and each paragraph is one or two sentences of 70-160 words that chain a definition, two or three sub-cases, a caveat and a recommendation with dashes and semicolons (q-12: 158 words, q-2: 137, q-13: 116, q-19: 95). 60.6% of EN sentences and 53.3% of RU sentences are over the length threshold. The content is right and the depth should stay — the fix is purely mechanical: split at the dashes and semicolons that are already there.
- The quiz bank was generated, never edited, and its explanations are structurally unusable. correctIndex is 0 in 18 of 20 items; the correct option is the longest option in 17 of 20 (EN) and 17 of 20 (RU), 15 of 20 in both locales at once — a reader can score well on this quiz without knowing any web performance. 10 explanation strings (5 items x 2 locales) refer to «Вариант 2»/'Option 2', which the runtime shuffle makes meaningless. 4 topics account for 14 of the 20 items (CLS x4, preload/prefetch x4, image formats x4, code splitting x2), and quiz-1 and quiz-11 are the same question with the same four options.
- Articles open by warming up instead of answering, then recover. 03-resource-loading and 06-rendering-performance both start with «Прежде чем говорить о… нужно понять…», and each article's final «Типичные ошибки на интервью» section is where all the over-long sentences in that file live (the 55-word fetchpriority bullet in en/03, 50-word content-visibility bullet in en/06, 54-word cache-invalidation bullet in en/07). Everything between those two ends — the body of every article — is the strongest writing in the zone: short sentences, an ASCII diagram or a ✅/❌ code pair after every single new idea.

**Прочее:** Quiz numbers requested: (a) longest option is correct in 17/20 EN and 17/20 RU, 15/20 in both locales simultaneously; (b) correctIndex distribution 0:18, 1:2, 2:0, 3:0; (c) 5 explanations contradict their own key, the articles or the bank — quiz-14 (JS vs CSS render-blocking, contradicts articles 02 and 08), quiz-9 (WebP as best compression, contradicts quiz-5, quiz-15 and article 08's ~30%/~50% figures), quiz-11 (FID described in present tense as a live metric, contradicts quiz-1, quiz-4 and article 01), quiz-16 (says options 2 and 3 both confuse CLS with another metric; only one does), quiz-2 ('ensures critical resources load first without blocking other assets', contradicts article 03 and bank q-2, which stress that preload competes for bandwidth and displaces other resources); (d) no unedited generation artifacts — no 'Wait, let me recalculate' or 'I apologize' strings in either locale — but 10 explanation strings do carry «Вариант N»/'Option N' references that the runtime shuffle breaks. Non-readability bugs worth a separate ticket: bank q-25 lists FID as a current Core Web Vital, which article 01 explicitly calls «признак несвежих знаний»; articles 01 and 08 disagree on whether INP is the 98th or 75th percentile; ru/01 line 77 «нет CDK» should be CDN; ru/03 line 20 «ЕЩЁНЕ»; ru/06 line 512 «видно WHERE происходят сдвиги»; ru/06 line 374 observes 'layout-shift' entries while the code checks entry.name === 'layout'; ru/04 line 191-200 declares const api twice and wraps a default export the worker snippet never creates.

## Все конкретные места «до / после»

Полный список от аудиторов, сгруппирован по зонам. Каждое «после» сохраняет все технические утверждения из «до» — правится только язык.

### agile-scrum (статьи)

**1. `content/topics/agile-scrum/en/07-antipatterns-and-lead-responsibilities.md` — критерий B**

*Проблема:* One 115-word sentence carrying four independent lead practices, separated only by semicolons, and each practice additionally carries its own 'do X rather than Y' contrast — so the reader has to hold eight clauses in working memory to reach the full stop. The content is already a list; the markup refuses to be one. On a phone this is roughly eight screen lines with no place to stop. This is the single longest sentence in the zone and the pattern repeats six times in this file alone.

До:

```
**What a lead does:** explicitly teaches the breakdown/spike/range technique from article 05 in 1:1s, rather than assuming a junior will pick it up on their own over time; reviews estimates together with the junior engineer before Sprint Planning for a while, rather than only after the estimate has already been said out loud in front of the whole team; normalizes the phrase "I don't know, let me run a spike" as a sign of professional maturity, not weakness; shares their own past estimation mistakes ("I once underestimated a similar integration by a week") — this removes the stigma of admitting uncertainty far better than any generic reassurance that "it's fine to be wrong."
```
После:

```
**What a lead does:**

- Teaches the breakdown / spike / range technique from article 05 explicitly, in 1:1s. Do not assume a junior will pick it up on their own over time.
- Reviews estimates together with the junior engineer before Sprint Planning, for a while — not only after the estimate has already been said out loud in front of the whole team.
- Normalizes the phrase "I don't know, let me run a spike." That is a sign of professional maturity, not weakness.
- Shares their own past estimation mistakes: "I once underestimated a similar integration by a week." This removes the stigma of admitting uncertainty far better than a generic "it's fine to be wrong."
```

**2. `content/topics/agile-scrum/ru/02-scrum-framework.md` — критерий B**

*Проблема:* 82 words (88 in en), one sentence, four causal steps chained with `→` inside running prose. The arrow is diagram notation used as punctuation: the reader cannot pause, and cannot see the chain, because it is laid out as a paragraph. This is the payoff section of the whole article ('Собранный пример') and it is the hardest thing to read in it. The file already uses ASCII blocks twice, so the idiom for showing a chain exists and is simply not used here.

До:

```
Одно деградировавшее событие редко существует изолированно — оно обычно тянет за собой остальные. Если Sprint Review — это формальная демонстрация без реальной обратной связи, то Product Backlog не адаптируется на основе реального пользовательского опыта → Sprint Planning продолжает выбирать задачи, ценность которых никто не проверял → Daily Scrum превращается в отчётность о выполнении заранее спущенного плана, а не в адаптацию к новой информации, потому что новой информации по сути и нет → Retrospective не может предложить осмысленных изменений, потому что корневая причина (нет реальной связи с пользователем) не обсуждается напрямую, а маскируется под операционные жалобы («у нас медленный CI»).
```
После:

```
Одно деградировавшее событие редко существует изолированно — оно обычно тянет за собой остальные. Вот эта цепочка по шагам:

1. Sprint Review — формальная демонстрация без реальной обратной связи.
2. Значит, Product Backlog не адаптируется на основе реального пользовательского опыта.
3. Значит, Sprint Planning продолжает выбирать задачи, ценность которых никто не проверял.
4. Значит, Daily Scrum превращается в отчётность о выполнении заранее спущенного плана. Адаптироваться не к чему: новой информации по сути нет.
5. Значит, Retrospective не может предложить осмысленных изменений. Корневая причина — нет реальной связи с пользователем — напрямую не обсуждается, а маскируется под операционные жалобы («у нас медленный CI»).
```

**3. `content/topics/agile-scrum/ru/06-scaling-and-frameworks.md` — критерий D**

*Проблема:* The reader's first encounter with SAFe is a single 44-word sentence introducing four organizational levels plus two brand-new abbreviations (ART, PI), with the definition of ART nested inside a parenthesis that itself contains the definition of PI. And this file is the only one in the zone with zero diagrams, zero tables and zero dialogues across ~1,100 words and four different scaling frameworks — so a structural, hierarchical idea gets no structural, hierarchical picture. Rubric D fails here harder than anywhere else in the zone, even though the file's own abbreviation hygiene is good.

До:

```
**SAFe** — предписывающий, многоуровневый фреймворк для масштабирования: уровень команды (обычная Scrum/Kanban-команда), уровень программы (**ART — Agile Release Train**, группа из нескольких команд, синхронизированных на общую каденцию, обычно **Program Increment (PI)** длиной 8–12 недель), уровень крупного решения и портфельный уровень (для координации между несколькими ART).
```
После:

```
**SAFe** — предписывающий фреймворк масштабирования: он раскладывает организацию на четыре уровня и синхронизирует их общим ритмом.

```txt
Портфель            координация между несколькими ART
└── Крупное решение
    └── Программа   ART: несколько команд на общей каденции,
        │           обычно Program Increment (PI) 8–12 недель
        └── Команда обычная Scrum- или Kanban-команда
```

**ART (Agile Release Train, «поезд релизов»)** — группа из нескольких команд, синхронизированных на общую каденцию. **PI (Program Increment, «инкремент программы»)** — этот общий отрезок времени, обычно 8–12 недель.
```

```
**What Kanban gives you in these conditions:** WIP limits keep the amount of work in progress under control no matter how many tickets actually arrive on a given day; flow metrics (cycle time, throughput) let you build probability-based SLA forecasts ("85% of tickets of this type close within 2 days") without needing to force work into artificial sprints; no required iteration means priority can shift instantly when reality changes, not only at a sprint boundary.

**What Kanban gives you in these conditions:**

- WIP limits keep the amount of work in progress under control, no matter how many tickets actually arrive on a given day.
- Flow metrics (cycle time, throughput) let you build probability-based SLA forecasts — "85% of tickets of this type close within 2 days" — without forcing work into artificial sprints.
- There is no required iteration, so priority can shift the moment reality changes, not only at a sprint boundary.

**9. `content/topics/agile-scrum/ru/03-kanban-and-flow.md` — критерий C**

*Проблема:* The article's first section is «Происхождение» and its first sentence is 52 words of Toyota history from the 1940s. The reader who opened the file to find out what Kanban *is* gets the answer in paragraph three («Это метод управления потоком работы»). The pyramid is inverted: essence should come first, origin after. Note this is also the second-longest sentence in the file, so the warm-up and the syntax defect compound.

До:

```
## Происхождение

Kanban («канбан», яп. 看板 — «вывеска», «сигнальная карточка») пришёл из Toyota Production System — производственной системы Toyota 1940–50-х годов, где сигнальные карточки использовались, чтобы регулировать поток деталей на конвейере: следующий этап производства запрашивал (pull) детали у предыдущего только тогда, когда у него реально была мощность их обработать, а не когда предыдущий этап их произвёл.
```
После:

```
## Что такое Kanban

Kanban — метод управления потоком работы: он ограничивает количество задач, находящихся в работе одновременно, и делает узкие места видимыми. В отличие от Scrum, это не фреймворк с фиксированным набором ролей и обязательных ритуалов — его можно наложить на любой существующий процесс.

### Откуда он взялся

Название пришло из Toyota Production System — производственной системы Toyota 1940–50-х годов (яп. 看板 — «вывеска», «сигнальная карточка»). Там сигнальные карточки регулировали поток деталей на конвейере: следующий этап производства запрашивал (pull) детали у предыдущего только тогда, когда у него реально была мощность их обработать, а не когда предыдущий этап их произвёл.
```

**11. `content/quiz/algorithms.json` — критерий C**

*Проблема:* algorithms-quiz-14. The explanation contains a live editorial artifact ("Wait, let me recalculate") — the reader watches the text change its mind mid-sentence and has no way to know which of the two answers is meant. Worse, the second attempt is arithmetically wrong: fib(5) = fib(4) + fib(3) = 3 + 2 = 5, not "5+3=8". The answer key is correctIndex=1 ("8"), so the marked-correct option is also wrong — the code in the question prints 5. A reader with no theory article to fall back on has literally nothing to correct this against. Same defect in ru (the "Wait" is dropped but "fib(5)=5+3=8" and the wrong key survive).

До:

```
The Fibonacci sequence starting from index 0 is: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8... So fib(5) = 5 (at index 5: 0→1→1→2→3→5→8). Wait, let me recalculate: fib(0)=0, fib(1)=1, fib(2)=1, fib(3)=2, fib(4)=3, fib(5)=5+3=8. The memoization optimization reduces redundant recursive calls from exponential to linear time complexity.
```
После:

```
The code prints 5. Counting from index 0, the sequence is fib(0)=0, fib(1)=1, fib(2)=1, fib(3)=2, fib(4)=3, fib(5)=5. Each value is the sum of the two before it, so fib(5) = fib(4) + fib(3) = 3 + 2 = 5. The `memo` dictionary stores each fib(k) the first time it is computed, so every value is computed once instead of being recomputed down two recursive branches. That turns the running time from exponential O(2^n) into linear O(n). (correctIndex must be changed to 0.)
```

**12. `content/quiz/algorithms.json` — критерий C**

*Проблема:* algorithms-quiz-16. The first sentence derives the right answer, O(n), and the second sentence then overturns it with a self-contradicting claim ("O(n) work on progressively smaller arrays" — it cannot be both O(n) per level and progressively smaller). The marked answer, correctIndex=0 = "O(n log n)", is wrong: the total work really is n + n/2 + n/4 + ... = 2n = O(n). The reader is taught a false rule about summing a geometric series — the exact skill this bank exists to teach. Identical in ru.

До:

```
The function processes n elements in the first call, then n/2 in the second, then n/4, etc., giving n + n/2 + n/4 + ... = O(n). However, the recursion depth is O(log n), and at each level we do O(n) work on progressively smaller arrays. This creates O(n log n) total complexity. Option B (O(n)) underestimates because it ignores the logarithmic depth of recursion.
```
После:

```
The answer is O(n). Each call loops once over its own array, then recurses on only the second half. So the work per call is n, then n/2, then n/4, and so on. Add them up: n + n/2 + n/4 + ... < 2n, which is O(n). Recursion depth is indeed O(log n), but that only counts the *number* of calls — it does not multiply the work, because each level is half the size of the one above. O(n log n) would be right only if every level did n work, as in merge sort. (correctIndex must be changed to 1.)
```

**13. `content/questions/algorithms.json` — критерий B**

*Проблема:* algorithms-q-38 (en; ru identical at 70 words). 72 words, four subordinate clauses, and the sentence states the same bound three times in a loop ("total O(n log n)" → "O(log n) amortized" → "total O(n log n)" → "matching the O(log n) amortized per-op bound"). The parenthetical "(not O(log n²))" is also malformed notation — O(log² n) is meant, and O(log n²) is actually equal to O(log n), so the disclaimer says nothing. A B1-B2 reader cannot hold this open long enough to parse it and has no theory article to check it against.

До:

```
So even though a single deletion can trigger O(log n) rotations, the *total* number of rotations across n operations is bounded by (total potential increase) which is O(n log n) worst case, but amortized per-operation the O(log n) height-fixing pass already dominates, giving O(log n) amortized (not O(log n²)) per operation — total O(n log n) for n operations, matching the O(log n) amortized per-op bound.
```
После:

```
Put the two halves together. Each operation adds at most O(log n) to the potential, so over n operations the potential rises by at most O(n log n) in total. Every rotation costs O(1) and consumes some of that potential, so all rotations together also cost at most O(n log n). Divide by n operations: O(log n) rotation cost per operation on average. That is the same order as the height-update pass each operation already pays, so nothing gets worse — the per-operation amortized cost stays O(log n), not O(log² n. A single deletion can still fire O(log n) rotations; the average over the whole sequence is what is bounded.
```

**14. `content/quiz/algorithms.json` — критерий C**

*Проблема:* algorithms-quiz-9. Options B ("BFS guarantees shortest path with O(V) space") and C ("BFS guarantees shortest path with O(V) queue space") are both true statements; the item asks for "most accurate" and then resolves the tie with a hand-wave the reader cannot verify. Compounding it: the explanation refers to "Option B" / "option C", but the four options are rendered as a plain list with no A/B/C/D labels, so the reader has to guess the mapping. This referencing habit appears in 12 of the 30 items, and the label style is not even consistent (algorithms-quiz-27 says "Option 1 ... Option 2 ... option 3", ru says «Вариант 1»; algorithms-quiz-10 says "Option A ... Option B", ru «Вариант A»).

До:

```
BFS explores level by level and guarantees the shortest path in unweighted graphs because it visits nodes in order of distance. The queue space is O(V) in worst case. DFS does not guarantee shortest path as it explores deeply first, potentially finding longer paths. Option B is imprecise about queue being the space requirement; option C correctly identifies BFS's guarantee.
```
После:

```
BFS guarantees the shortest path in an unweighted graph, and the memory it needs is the queue, which holds O(V) nodes in the worst case. BFS works because it visits nodes in order of distance from the source: everything one step away, then everything two steps away, and so on. So the first time it reaches the target, it cannot have taken a longer route. DFS goes as deep as it can before backing up, so the first route it finds to the target is often not the shortest. The other answers either name DFS as the one with the guarantee, or claim both traversals have it. (Options B and C should be rewritten so only one of them is true — as written both are correct statements.)
```

```

The shifting is the clever part. When you go down one row, you shift `diag1` left by one and `diag2` right by one. Same geometry, just packed into machine words instead of hash-set entries.

**17. `content/quiz/algorithms.json` — критерий G**

*Проблема:* algorithms-quiz-21 (ru). «Термин» is a false-friend translation of "term" — in Russian a summand in an expression is «слагаемое» or «член», never «термин» (which means "a term of art"). A junior reader is left to work out that «доминирующий термин» is not a piece of vocabulary. This is the sharpest instance of a calqued layer that runs through the whole quiz ru file but is absent from the question-bank ru: «пространство» is used 23 times where Russian says «память» ("O(log n) вспомогательным пространством", "компромисс пространство-время" 9×), plus «коллидируют» (quiz-2), «приоритизируется над памятью» (quiz-24), «bucket» in quiz-2 versus «бакет» in quiz-15, and quiz-9 renders "unweighted graph" as «неориентированном графе без весов», adding an undirectedness claim the en does not make.

До:

```
При объединении операций мы оставляем доминирующий термин. O(n²) из вложенных циклов доминирует над O(n log n) из цикла бинарного поиска, поэтому общая сложность составляет O(n²). Постоянные множители и члены более низкого порядка отбрасываются в нотации Big O.
```
После:

```
Когда операции идут одна за другой, оставляем самое быстрорастущее слагаемое. Вложенные циклы дают O(n²), цикл с бинарным поиском — O(n log n). При больших n первое растёт быстрее, поэтому оно и определяет ответ: O(n²). В нотации Big O постоянные множители и слагаемые меньшего порядка отбрасываются.
```

**18. `content/questions/algorithms.json` — критерий D**

*Проблема:* algorithms-q-36 (en and ru). Two list items introduce six unexplained concepts in a row: odd-degree vertex, handshake lemma, minimum-weight perfect matching, multigraph, even degree, Eulerian circuit — plus a proof sketch compressed into a parenthesis. Nothing is grounded in an example and the final line then uses `OPT` as a symbol that is never introduced ("Total cost ≤ MST + matching ≤ OPT + OPT/2 = 1.5 * OPT"). MST is expanded on first use one line earlier, which makes the omission of OPT more jarring. With no theory article behind this bank, every one of those six terms is a stop-and-google.

До:

```
2. Find odd-degree vertices in the MST (always an even count, by handshake lemma) and compute a minimum-weight perfect matching among them — cost ≤ half the optimal tour (proven via triangle inequality applied to the optimal tour split into two matchings).
3. Combine MST + matching into a multigraph — every vertex now has even degree, guaranteeing an Eulerian circuit exists.
```
После:

```
2. Look at the vertices of the MST that have an odd number of edges. There is always an even number of them (every edge adds 1 to two vertices, so the degrees sum to an even number — the handshake lemma). Pair those odd vertices up so that every one of them gets exactly one partner and the total weight of the pairs is as small as possible; this is called a minimum-weight perfect matching. Its cost is at most half the optimal tour: the optimal tour visits these vertices in some cyclic order, and splitting that cycle into alternating edges gives two matchings, so the cheaper one costs at most half.
3. Add those matching edges on top of the MST. Because each odd vertex just gained one more edge, every vertex now has an even number of edges. A connected graph where every vertex has even degree has an Eulerian circuit — a closed walk that uses every edge exactly once. (Write `OPT` out on first use: "call the total weight of the optimal tour OPT".)
```

*Проблема:* The opening clause «Зачем это нужно ровно настолько, насколько сложно» does not parse — it is trying to say «оно стоит своей сложности», but as written there is no verb and no comparison the reader can resolve. До:

```
Зачем это нужно ровно настолько, насколько сложно: DI даёт **подменяемость** (в тестах вместо HTTP-сервиса подставляется мок — без моканья модулей), **область жизни** (один инстанс на приложение, на маршрут или на компонент — решается конфигурацией, а не кодом сервиса) и **конфигурируемость** (значения из окружения раздаются через токены, а не импортируются напрямую).
```
После:

```
DI (dependency injection, внедрение зависимостей) — сложный механизм, и он окупает свою сложность тремя вещами.

- **Подменяемость.** В тестах вместо HTTP-сервиса подставляется мок, и моканье модулей не нужно.
- **Область жизни.** Один инстанс на приложение, на маршрут или на компонент. Это решается конфигурацией, а не кодом самого сервиса.
- **Конфигурируемость.** Значения из окружения раздаются через токены, а не импортируются напрямую.
```

**22. `content/courses/angular/en/04-dependency-injection.md` — критерий F**

*Проблема:* 55 words, and the lead clause is an idiom a B1-B2 reader cannot decode: "it is worth exactly as much as it costs" is not standard English and gives no information — the reader spends the sentence trying to work out whether DI is being praised or criticised. Three peer items are then packed into one sentence with three parenthetical asides and two em-dashes. On a phone the parentheses wrap and the three items stop being visually separable.

До:

```
It is worth exactly as much as it costs: DI gives you **substitutability** (a mock replaces the HTTP service in tests — no module mocking), **lifetime** (one instance per application, per route or per component — decided by configuration, not by the service's code) and **configurability** (environment values are handed out through tokens rather than imported directly).
```
После:

```
DI (dependency injection) is a complex mechanism, and it pays that complexity back in three ways.

- **Substitutability.** In tests a mock replaces the HTTP service, with no module mocking.
- **Lifetime.** One instance per application, per route or per component. Configuration decides this, not the service's own code.
- **Configurability.** Environment values are handed out through tokens instead of being imported directly.
```

**23. `content/courses/angular/en/00-angular-model-and-setup.md` — критерий B**

*Проблема:* 62 words, the longest sentence in the zone, and roughly fifteen API names the reader has never seen and cannot evaluate — on page one of the course. The comma levels are ambiguous: `signal queries (stabilized in v20)` could attach to the signal group or to the whole list. A reader cannot tell whether this must be learned now or skimmed, because it is written as prose rather than as the reference card it actually is.

До:

```
**Stable and the main path:** standalone components (the default since v19), `inject()`, the new control flow `@if`/`@for`/`@switch`/`@let`, `@defer`, functional guards and interceptors, and all signal-based reactivity — `signal`, `computed`, `effect`, `linkedSignal`, signal-based `input()`/`output()`/`model()` and signal queries (stabilized in v20), async reactivity via `resource()`/`httpResource`, and Signal Forms (stabilized in v22), plus the esbuild/Vite build system (`@angular/build`).
```
После:

```
**Stable and the main path.** Skim this list now and come back to it — every item gets its own chapter.

  - Standalone components — the default since v19.
  - `inject()`, plus functional guards and interceptors.
  - The new control flow: `@if`, `@for`, `@switch`, `@let`, `@defer`.
  - Signal reactivity: `signal`, `computed`, `effect`, `linkedSignal`, the signal-based `input()`/`output()`/`model()`, and signal queries. All of it stabilized in v20.
  - Async reactivity: `resource()` and `httpResource`. Signal Forms. Both stabilized in v22.
  - The esbuild/Vite build system (`@angular/build`).
```

**24. `content/courses/angular/en/03-change-detection.md` — критерий B**

*Проблема:* 64 words — a three-item list written as one sentence, with a fourth option smuggled into item (c) after an "or". This is the zone's single repeating structural habit and it is at its worst here: the reader is asked to hold three parallel mechanisms in memory across two semicolons while each item also carries its own dash-clause explanation. The Russian version has the identical shape at 49 words.

До:

```
Three ways: (a) replace the mutation with creating a new object — then the input comparison sees a new reference and the child is checked; (b) keep the state in a signal and read it in the child's template — the signal notifies regardless of inputs; (c) call `markForCheck()` on the child (for example by reaching it through `viewChild`) or give the child the `Eager` strategy.
```
После:

```
Three ways:

  - **Replace the mutation with a new object.** The input comparison then sees a new reference, so the child is checked.
  - **Keep the state in a signal and read it in the child's template.** The signal notifies regardless of inputs.
  - **Force the check from outside.** Call `markForCheck()` on the child — for example by reaching it through `viewChild` — or give the child the `Eager` strategy.
```

**29. `content/courses/angular/ru/03-change-detection.md` — критерий D**

*Проблема:* Four new concepts are named and none is explained: the reader learns the phase names and their order, is told two of the four should be avoided, and is never told what any of them does. The example above uses only `read` and `write`, so `earlyRead` and `mixedReadWrite` have no anchor at all. On top of that «layout trashing» is a misspelling of "layout thrashing" (the EN file spells it correctly) and is left untranslated and unexplained, so the one sentence that justifies the whole design is the one the reader cannot decode.

До:

```
`afterRenderEffect` стабилен и имеет четыре фазы — `earlyRead`, `write`, `mixedReadWrite`, `read` — которые выполняются в этом порядке и только если эффект «грязный». Разделение фаз нужно, чтобы не порождать layout trashing: сначала все чтения, потом все записи. `mixedReadWrite` и `earlyRead` документация советует избегать.
```
После:

```
`afterRenderEffect` стабилен. У него четыре фазы, и они выполняются строго в этом порядке — и только если эффект «грязный»:

- `earlyRead` — чтение layout до записей (нужно редко);
- `write` — изменения DOM;
- `mixedReadWrite` — чтение и запись вперемешку;
- `read` — чтение layout после всех записей.

Зачем это разделение. Если чередовать чтение и запись layout, браузер вынужден пересчитывать раскладку на каждом чтении — это называется layout thrashing («пробуксовка раскладки») и заметно тормозит. Фазы гарантируют порядок «сначала все записи, потом все чтения». Документация советует избегать `mixedReadWrite` и `earlyRead` — именно потому, что они этот порядок размывают.
```

**30. `content/courses/angular/ru/07-routing.md` — критерий E**

*Проблема:* Ten API names in one sentence with no lead, no grouping and no criterion for choosing between them — four of them carry option objects the reader has never seen. A separate problem in this chapter: the theory block declares the ticket routes as nested `children: [{ path: 'new' }, { path: ':id' }]`, while the solution walkthrough declares them as flat siblings `path: 'tickets/new'` and `path: 'tickets/:id'`. Both carry the same comment about order mattering, but they are different route shapes and nothing acknowledges the switch, so a reader following the chapter end-to-end cannot tell which one the exercise expects.

До:

```
Полезные фичи `provideRouter`: `withComponentInputBinding()`, `withViewTransitions()` (анимация через View Transitions API), `withInMemoryScrolling({ scrollPositionRestoration: 'enabled', anchorScrolling: 'enabled' })`, `withRouterConfig({ onSameUrlNavigation: 'reload' })`, `withHashLocation()`, `withNavigationErrorHandler(fn)`, `withDebugTracing()`.
```
После:

```
Фичи `provideRouter` — справочник, к которому стоит вернуться при настройке проекта.

Что нужно почти всегда:

- `withComponentInputBinding()` — параметры маршрута попадают во входы компонента;
- `withInMemoryScrolling({ scrollPositionRestoration: 'enabled', anchorScrolling: 'enabled' })` — восстановление позиции скролла при возврате назад и переход к якорю.

Что нужно по случаю:

- `withViewTransitions()` — анимация перехода через View Transitions API;
- `withRouterConfig({ onSameUrlNavigation: 'reload' })` — переход на тот же URL перезапускает маршрут;
- `withHashLocation()` — адреса вида `/#/tickets`, когда сервер не умеет отдавать index.html на любой путь;
- `withNavigationErrorHandler(fn)` — единая обработка упавших навигаций;
- `withDebugTracing()` — лог всех этапов навигации в консоль, только для отладки.
```

```

Затем проверьте в Lighthouse, что не вырос CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift) — метрика того, насколько сильно вёрстка «прыгает» во время загрузки.

**32. `content/courses/angular/en/15-build-deploy-and-capstone.md` — критерий F**

*Проблема:* 68 words, two labelled branches and three inline dashes in one sentence. Worse, 'stand' is a calque of Russian «стенд»: in English a deployment target is an environment, and 'stand' reads as nonsense. It appears four times in en/15 ('when the stand changes', 'builds for two stands', 'which stand the code was built for', 'on the real stand').

До:

```
A token is an extension point: (a) in tests the config is supplied by a provider (`provideAppConfig({ apiUrl: '/api' })`), so tests do not depend on which stand the code was built for (chapter 13); (b) the value can be obtained at runtime — from `index.html`, from a server response, from an environment variable through `define` — so one artifact can be deployed to several stands with no rebuild.
```
После:

```
A token is an extension point, and that buys you two things. First, tests: the config comes from a provider, `provideAppConfig({ apiUrl: '/api' })`, so a test no longer depends on which environment the code was built for (chapter 13). Second, runtime: the value can arrive from `index.html`, from a server response, or from `define`. One build artifact then deploys to staging and to production without a rebuild.
```

**33. `content/courses/angular/ru/09-rxjs-in-angular.md` — критерий E**

*Проблема:* `this.router` is never declared in this `TicketForm` class — the only fields are `api` and `submit$`. `Subject`, `exhaustMap` and `TicketDto` have no import line either. The chapter's own exercise (point 5) asks the reader to build exactly this, so the snippet is the reference answer, and it does not compile. Identical defect in en/09.

До:

```
export class TicketForm {
  private readonly api = inject(TicketApi);
  private readonly submit$ = new Subject<TicketDto>();

  constructor() {
    this.submit$
      .pipe(
        exhaustMap((dto) => this.api.create(dto)),
        takeUntilDestroyed(),
      )
      .subscribe(() => void this.router.navigate(['/tickets']));
  }
```
После:

```
import { Subject, exhaustMap } from 'rxjs';
import { Router } from '@angular/router';

export class TicketForm {
  private readonly api = inject(TicketApi);
  private readonly router = inject(Router);
  private readonly submit$ = new Subject<TicketDto>();

  constructor() {
    this.submit$
      .pipe(
        exhaustMap((dto) => this.api.create(dto)),
        takeUntilDestroyed(),
      )
      .subscribe(() => void this.router.navigate(['/tickets']));
  }
```

**39. `content/courses/angular/en/12-performance.md` — критерий B**

*Проблема:* 56 words, three semicolon-separated items each carrying its own dash clause, and no finite verb until the very end of items two and three. On a phone this is roughly eight lines with no place to stop. The RU original is 46 words and has the same shape, so the fix applies to both.

До:

```
On by default: zoneless change detection (since v21) — checks happen only on explicit notifications instead of walking the whole tree on every async operation; `OnPush` for components (since v22) — a component is checked only when its inputs changed, an event occurred, or a signal read in its template changed; and signals as the fine-grained notification mechanism.

После:

```
Three things are on by default. Zoneless change detection, since v21: Angular checks only on an explicit notification, instead of walking the whole tree after every async operation. `OnPush` for components, since v22: a component is checked only when its inputs changed, an event fired in it, or a signal its template reads changed. And signals themselves, as the mechanism that sends those notifications precisely where they are needed.
```

### angular (вопросы)

**41. `content/questions/angular.json#en` — критерий F**

*Проблема:* angular-q-102, English. 56 words, the longest sentence in the bank. Two independent causal chains joined by a semicolon plus a dash-clause verdict at the end. A B1-B2 reader has to hold the first half in memory across the semicolon while parsing 'incorporates state that changes independently of the item'. The Russian version of the same sentence is 46 words and also over the limit, but the English one adds a third clause. Nothing here is conceptually hard — it is one sentence doing three jobs.

До:

```
The expression runs for every item on every diff, so a costly helper turns an O(n) comparison into something noticeably slower; and if the key incorporates state that changes independently of the item, every change to that state invalidates the entire list and forces a full re-creation — the exact opposite of what `track` is for.
```
После:

```
The expression runs for every item on every diff. So a costly helper turns an O(n) comparison into something noticeably slower. There is a second, worse failure. If the key contains state that changes on its own, separately from the item, then every change to that state makes every key look new. Angular then re-creates the whole list — the exact opposite of what `track` is for.
```

**42. `content/questions/angular.json#en` — критерий F**

*Проблема:* angular-q-58, English. 52 words with a mid-sentence quoted phrase, a compound predicate ('keeps working ... and starts showing'), a dash-clause restriction, and a trailing 'which' clause that refers back to the whole thing. The reader has to reconstruct the subject after 30 words of intervening material. The Russian equivalent is 50 words and has the same shape, so this is a shared structural habit, not a translation artefact.

До:

```
A codebase where components hold plain fields and rely on "Angular checks after every event" keeps working under zone.js and starts showing stale UI the moment zone.js is removed — and only on the paths that mutate outside a signal or an event handler, which makes it look intermittent rather than systematic.
```
После:

```
Take a codebase where components hold plain fields and rely on "Angular checks after every event". It keeps working under zone.js. It starts showing stale UI the moment zone.js is removed. And it breaks only on the paths that mutate outside a signal or an event handler. That is why the failure looks intermittent rather than systematic.

**48. `content/questions/angular.json#en` — критерий E**

*Проблема:* angular-q-95 (advanced, accessibility). The block is four unrelated fragments in one fence, and three identifiers are never defined: `this.items`, `this.host`, and `el`. Worse, the last two lines are bare `inject(LiveAnnouncer).announce(...)` and `inject(FocusMonitor).monitor(el)` statements with no enclosing class or field initialiser — which contradicts this bank's own rule from q-15 that `inject()` only works in an injection context. A reader who copies this gets NG0203. This is the only code block in 104 answers that is not self-contained; everywhere else the code is exemplary.

До:

```
// keyboard navigation over a list, with wrap-around and type-ahead
private readonly keyManager = new ActiveDescendantKeyManager(this.items)
  .withWrap()
  .withTypeAhead();

// announce a change to screen readers
inject(LiveAnnouncer).announce(`${this.count()} tickets found`);
```
После:

```
export class TicketList {
  private readonly items = viewChildren(TicketRow);
  private readonly host = viewChild.required<ElementRef>('list');

  // keyboard navigation over a list, with wrap-around and type-ahead
  private readonly keyManager = new ActiveDescendantKeyManager(this.items())
    .withWrap()
    .withTypeAhead();

  // inject() only works here, at field initialisation (see the inject() question)
  private readonly announcer = inject(LiveAnnouncer);

  onFiltered(): void {
    // announce a change to screen readers
    this.announcer.announce(`${this.count()} tickets found`);
  }
}
```

### architecture (статьи+вопросы+quiz)

**51. `content/questions/architecture.json#en` — критерий B**

*Проблема:* 74 words, one sentence, in architecture-q-3. It carries five separate facts (generic interface is fine for CRUD; three kinds of query break it; consequence A bloat; consequence B bypass; what real codebases do) joined by 'but / once / either-or / anyway - so'. On a phone this is roughly seven lines with no place to stop. CRUD and ORM are also both unexpanded at their first use in this file.

До:

```
Where it falls short: a generic `IRepository<T>` interface works well for simple CRUD, but once you need complex queries with joins, pagination, or aggregation specific to one use case, forcing them through a generic interface either bloats it with dozens of specialized methods or pushes people to bypass the repository and query the ORM directly anyway - so most real codebases add specialized query methods per repository rather than keeping it purely generic.
```
После:

```
Where it falls short: a generic `IRepository<T>` interface works well for simple CRUD (create, read, update, delete). It stops working once one use case needs a complex query - a join, pagination, or an aggregation. You then have two bad options. Either you bloat the generic interface with dozens of specialized methods, or people bypass the repository and query the ORM (object-relational mapper) directly. Most real codebases take a third route: keep the generic base thin and add specialized query methods to each concrete repository.
```

**53. `content/quiz/architecture.json#en` — критерий C**

*Проблема:* architecture-quiz-9. A reader who is learning the vocabulary now has two opposite words for one concept inside a single screen, and no way to tell which is the site's term.

До:

Layered Architecture is fundamentally different—it relies on strict vertical separation and doesn't inherently invert dependencies, making it more prone to tight coupling between layers.
```
После:

```
Layered Architecture is different: it stacks horizontal layers and only fixes the call order (each layer calls the one below). It does not invert dependencies, so a layer can still import the concrete class beneath it and become tightly coupled to it.
```

**54. `content/questions/architecture.json#en` — критерий B**

*Проблема:* 72 words in architecture-q-24. It is a three-item list written as one sentence with semicolons. 'the entire constellation of services' is also a dead metaphor that costs the B1-B2 reader a re-read.

До:

```
Concrete signs you're looking at one: you can't deploy service A without also deploying service B in the same release window; a full regression test requires spinning up the entire constellation of services, not just the one you changed; and there's no way to answer "what does this service depend on" without reading five other codebases, because the dependency isn't declared anywhere - it's just implicit in call chains and shared tables.

После:

```
Three concrete signs you are looking at one:\n\n- You cannot deploy service A without deploying service B in the same release window.\n- A full regression test needs every service running, not just the one you changed.\n- Nobody can answer "what does this service depend on" without reading five other codebases. The dependency is declared nowhere - it only exists in call chains and shared tables.
```

*Проблема:* This is the opening of a 164-word, 17-line paragraph inside a 4,443-word file that contains zero fenced code blocks and zero diagrams - the only one of the eight articles with none. До:

```
Problems: (1) **Latency multiplication** — if each downstream call takes 50ms and is sequential, the request takes 400ms minimum. Parallel calls help but don't eliminate the problem. (2) **Cascading failures** — …  Fixes in increasing scope: (a) **Parallelize independent calls** with `Promise.all` … (d) **Reconsider service boundaries** …
```
После:

```
**Problems**\n\n- **Latency multiplication.** Each downstream call takes 50ms. Eight sequential calls means the request takes 400ms at minimum. Running them in parallel helps, but does not remove the problem.\n- **Cascading failures.** If any one of the 8 services goes down or slows, the orchestrating service degrades or fails with it - unless you have circuit breakers.\n\n(…then the fixes as their own bullet list, and a 6-line `Promise.all` + `opossum` snippet under the first two fixes, matching the format of articles 01-07.)
```

`await db.save(order); await broker.publish('OrderCreated', order)` looks correct and passes every happy-path test, but it's two unrelated writes with no shared atomicity guarantee. … Both are rare enough to pass code review and demo fine, and common enough to show up as a real incident within months at any meaningful throughput.

### aws (статьи)

**61. `content/topics/aws/ru/11-aws-interview-questions.md` — критерий A**

*Проблема:* Five opaque acronyms in one 17-word sentence, none of them expanded anywhere in this file: EC2, ECS, STS, TTL (and IAM in the sentence before). This is the highest-traffic file in the zone (1366 words, the question bank people revise from) and it expands nothing — 23+ acronyms arrive cold. The reader has to leave the page to learn that STS is a token-issuing service and TTL is a lifetime, which are exactly the two facts the sentence depends on.

До:

```
IAM Role — набор permissions с Trust Policy (кто может принять роль). Lambda/EC2/ECS принимают роль через STS → получают временные credentials (AccessKeyId + SecretAccessKey + SessionToken, TTL 1-12ч).
```
После:

```
IAM Role (роль) — это набор прав плюс Trust Policy: описание того, кто имеет право эту роль взять. Взять роль могут сервисы: Lambda, EC2 (виртуальные машины) и ECS (контейнеры). Они делают это через STS (Security Token Service — сервис выдачи временных ключей). В ответ приходят временные credentials: AccessKeyId, SecretAccessKey и SessionToken. Живут они от 1 до 12 часов — это их TTL (time to live, срок жизни).
```

## Паттерн 1: статический SPA / статический экспорт Next.js

Самая простая и дешёвая схема из всех семи: собранные файлы лежат в S3, а раздаёт их пользователям CloudFront. Своего сервера нет вообще. Подходит для SPA (Single Page Application — приложение, которое целиком грузится в браузер и дальше рисует страницы само).
